samples.question: The figure shows one survey panel on off-white paper. Exactly one mark is pure black: a single thick black route that descends continuously from its upper end to its lower end and never rises back up, so at every height it has exactly one horizontal position. Follow that black route from its upper end to its lower end. A reversal is a place where the route stops moving to the left and starts moving to the right, or the other way round. Every reversal in this figure is a wide swing: the route travels at least twenty pixels horizontally on each side of it, and the route contains no smaller wiggles, so every direction change counts. Count every reversal along the whole route, including all of the ones in its middle. The thin coloured curves, the grey rectangle, the grey tick marks and the two small grey squares at the route's ends are decoration and carry no information. How many reversals does the black route make? Answer with one number: 2, 3, 4, or 5.
